title: Lewis Miley signs new six-year Newcastle contract
content:
Newcastle United midfielder Lewis Miley has signed a new six-year contract with the club.

The new terms will tie the 20-year-old academy graduate down at St James’ Park until 2032.

The England Under-21 international made 34 appearances in all competitions this season, including filling in admirably at right-back while Eddie Howe’s side battled injuries.

He missed the final three matches of the campaign after suffering a broken leg in training but is expected to be back for the club’s pre-season later this summer.

“I’m really pleased to sign this new contract and commit my future here,” Miley said. “It’s a dream to be representing Newcastle United, so this is a proud moment for me.

“I’m really grateful to everybody who has played a part in helping me get to where I am today, especially the support of my family and the trust that the club has put in me from such a young age.

“It’s been an amazing journey so far and I’m so excited for what’s ahead. I’m now working hard every day to get back on the pitch even stronger next season and start to repay
the faith that has been shown in me.”

“Lewis fully deserves his new contract as recognition for everything he has achieved over the last few years,” Howe added. “It’s also a reflection of the potential for further growth that we all see in him.

“He’s earned every opportunity and has proven himself to be more than capable of performing at the highest level. Players like Lewis are a dream to work with — not only is he immensely talented, he’s keen to learn and approaches everything with a brilliant attitude.

“His versatility has proven to be a major plus and his willingness to try new roles is a reflection of his selfless approach to the team. I’m really looking forward to seeing Lewis back in action next season and I’m confident he will continue to go from strength to strength.”

Analysis from Newcastle correspondent George Caulkin

After a challenging season for Newcastle, the summer begins with a jolt of positive news and also a signpost as to what comes next.

Miley is ready. Still only 20, the academy graduate should no longer be thought of as fine prospect, but as a mainstay and the kind of player you can build a team around.

Versatile, adept, with a fantastic football brain and great technical quality, Miley has the lot. Newcastle could have done with him at Fulham on Sunday, where Sandro Tonali was a late absentee with injury and Howe began with no recognised right-back in his team. Miley is a natural in both positions.

But they need him full stop. He is Newcastle’s crown jewel; all the more pity that the last few months have been bitty thanks to injury. He is now recovering from a fractured fibula.

Buying young will be a feature of Newcastle’s transfer activity this summer. They have an aging, waning team which is in serious need of uplift and this policy comes with promise as well as pitfalls. There are no guarantees and development can take time and patience.

Yet Miley, Will Osula, Lewis Hall and others show what Howe can do when given the time to do it. Throw a few more like this into the mix and perhaps, just perhaps, excitement lies ahead.
